question.text: Scenario: Vikram Patel invested Rs.5,00,000 in DEF Equity Fund on March 15. He submitted his redemption request for the entire holding on April 5 (a Monday, working day) before the 3:00 PM cutoff. The following events occurred: Event 1: By April 9 (Friday, with no holidays in between), Vikram had not received his redemption proceeds in his bank account. Event 2: He called the AMC's customer care on April 9 and was told the delay was due to 'technical issues at the RTA' and that the proceeds would be credited within 2 more working days. Event 3: By April 13 (Tuesday), the proceeds were still not received. Vikram sent an email complaint to the AMC. Event 4: The AMC responded on April 16 (Friday) saying the RTA has been instructed to process the payment and it should arrive by April 20. Event 5: On April 20, Vikram received only Rs.4,85,000 instead of the expected Rs.4,97,500 (based on the redemption NAV and units held). He was not given any explanation for the shortfall of Rs.12,500. Question 4 of 5: Regarding the shortfall of Rs.12,500 in redemption proceeds, what should Vikram verify?

answer.text: Whether the AMC deducted TDS since Vikram is a resident Indian redeeming an equity fund
Whether the scheme changed its fundamental attributes during the holding period
Whether stamp duty was charged on the redemption
Whether exit load was deducted, whether STT was applied, and whether the applied NAV matches the NAV as of the redemption date — by requesting an itemised redemption statement from the RTA/AMC

explanation.text: The Logic: The shortfall could be due to (1) exit load, if the scheme has one and the holding period is within the load window — relevant here because the investment date is March 15 and the redemption date is April 5; (2) STT on equity-oriented redemptions; (3) the applied NAV differing from what Vikram expected. Vikram should request an itemised redemption statement from the RTA/AMC showing applied NAV, exit load, STT and any other disclosed charge so each component can be checked. Stamp duty applies to issue/inflow transactions, not to redemptions, and resident-Indian redemption proceeds from an equity scheme are not subject to TDS. The Trap: Assuming stamp duty or resident TDS explains the gap is wrong. Equally, asserting that 1% exit load plus STT explains a Rs.12,500 shortfall on Rs.4,97,500 (~2.5%) is mathematically inconsistent — 1% exit load plus 0.001% STT is roughly 1% in total — so do not pre-attribute the gap without the itemised breakup. Note: Source: NISM Series II-B (RTA Mutual Fund) workbook (exit load and itemised statements) and NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook (STT on equity-fund redemptions, stamp duty on inflows only, no resident TDS on equity redemptions).
